acceptance: Each numbered gap is either fixed with a test that fails before the fix, or closed with a recorded reason it is not worth fixing.
Gap 1: a branch worktree holding an ignored file that is not a known tool temp file is held by worktree-finish and worktree-reap, as a detached one already is.

Gap 2: after a force-push to origin/release/<major>.<minor>.x, a detached worktree integrated into the new line tip is removable without a manual git fetch --prune, and one integrated only into the old tip stays held.

Gap 6: decide whether to accept only the main worktree (the first git worktree list entry) as an override; that changes test_preflight_rejects_primary_clone_without_override, so it needs the owner's approval first.

Guardrails: never remove a worktree with --force; never unlock a worktree someone else locked; BENCHBOX_ALLOW_MAIN_CLONE_WRITE=1 still bypasses the primary-clone checks; snapshot format stays readable by the current check.
description:
Independent reviews of the primary-clone preflight hardening (PR #4323), the stray-override fix (PR #4353) and the release-line and detached-worktree reaping change (PR #4330) found these gaps. They are low risk and none is a regression; the owner chose on 2026-11-18 to track them together, not fix them in those PRs.

1. scripts/worktree_finish.py checks a detached worktree for ignored files that are not tool temp files before removing it, but a branch worktree gets no such check, so ignored data files in a branch worktree are removed with it.
2. Release-line refs are fetched without a + refspec. After a release branch is force-pushed, the fetch fails, so detached worktrees integrated into that line stay held until git fetch --prune runs. This is safe but leaves them behind.
3. A gap of a few milliseconds remains between the HEAD re-check at apply time and git worktree remove for a detached worktree; a commit made in that window would be lost from the worktree but stay in the object store until gc.
4. scripts/check_primary_clone_clean.sh creates temp files without a trap, so an interrupted run leaves them in the temp directory.
5. Primary-clone snapshots recorded before PR #4323 stored files with quoted names as deleted, so such a file is reported once after the upgrade. BENCHBOX_PRIMARY_SNAPSHOT_REFRESH=1 or a new session clears it.
6. BENCHBOX_AGENT_PRIMARY_CLONE is still honoured when it names another existing worktree of the same repository, so exporting it from inside an agent's own worktree would hide primary-clone writes. test_preflight_rejects_primary_clone_without_override relies on this.
